summary: Simulates spring/mass vibration per channel, using input as desired position or applied force with spring, mass, damping, and reset controls.
key_concepts: Spring CHOP creates vibration as if each channel were a mass attached to a spring.
In position mode, the input channel is the desired position and the previous output is the actual position.
In force mode, the input is applied as force to the spring/mass system rather than a target position.
Spring Constant, Mass, and Damping Constant determine oscillation frequency, amplitude, resistance, and settling behavior.
Initial conditions can come from the channel start or from explicit initial position and speed parameters.
The official docs recommend feeding step-like values and adjusting constants to understand and tune the response.

key_params.name: springk
key_params.note: Spring strength; higher values increase oscillation frequency

key_params.name: mass
key_params.note: Mass value; higher values lower frequency and resist damping

key_params.name: method
key_params.note: Interpret input as position or force

key_params.name: condfromchan
key_params.note: Initialize position and velocity from the beginning of the channel

common_gotchas: Position mode treats input as desired position; force mode treats input as an applied force.
In force mode, zero force tends to stabilize around zero rather than the previous target position.
Higher damping settles faster but can remove the desired bounce.
Initial conditions matter for repeatability when generating procedural motion.
Reset state before replaying deterministic generated animations.
Step-like Constant CHOP inputs are useful for tuning the spring response.
Higher mass can increase amplitude and resist damping, so mass and damping should be tuned together.
